summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and created a new worktree. It never ran `sdd-state register` or `sdd-state next`. Instead it wrote its session line into progress.md by hand with `cat >>`, then tried `sdd-state claim ... 1`, which returned "status=held ... exit=4". It then stopped and asked me which task to take. After my scripted "No, the other session is still working." it handed back a second time without claiming Task 2. Only after I sent "yes, go ahead" did it claim Task 2, implement and review it, and mark it complete. It never used --takeover.
reasoning: Criteria 1 and 4 pass. Criteria 2, 3 and 5 fail. The held-task rule is the point of this scenario: a session that finds a task held should take the claimable one without stopping. The agent never used register or next. It tried to claim the held Task 1 first, then handed back to the user twice. It took Task 2 only after an extra confirmation. The ledger also lacks a 'Task 2: branch' line.

observations.description: The agent skipped the `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next` verbs. It joined the ledger by appending a hand-written session line to progress.md with `cat >>`, using a made-up timestamp (15:10:00Z). This bypasses the state tooling.
The agent claimed Task 1 first (`sdd-state claim ... 1`), even though the user said the other session holds Task 1. It got exit=4 'held'. It never asked the state tool which task was claimable.

The agent stopped twice at the held task. It said 'the skill doesn't let me choose which tasks run concurrently' and asked the user for a task split. After being told the other session is still working, it still refused to take the only claimable task (Task 2) without explicit permission.
The ledger has no 'Task 2: branch' line. The branch only appears inside the 'Task 2: implementer ...' line.

In the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs, 'No, exit' is selected by default. Claude Code also offered to switch the pinned 'Opus 5' to Opus 5.5, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I declined.

Claude Code refused a compound Bash command ('names git in a form too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree'). The agent had to split it into separate commands, which is extra friction in worktree-isolated sessions.

The implementer subagent added a Co-Authored-By trailer naming 'Claude Haiku 4.5' with no blank line before it. The agent logged this as a deferred minor item. The Codex review gate was skipped because codex-plugin-cc is not installed.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development via the Skill tool before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: the first tool call is "Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development". The screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" before any Bash or Agent call.

criteria.criterion: Ran `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next`; the next output names Task 2 as claimable
criteria.evidence: I searched the Bash commands in the session log for `sdd-state (register|next)` and got 0 matches. The only sdd-state verbs it used were sync, verify, claim 1, snapshot, claim 2, snapshot. It registered by hand-appending to the ledger: `cat >> .../progress.md <<'EOF' session 13f143b1-...: mode worktree on worktree-parallel-session-2 ...`. No `next` output exists.

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with `sdd-state claim ... 2 --session ...` and worked it; the ledger holds a `Task 2: branch` line
criteria.evidence: The claim command was in the log: `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 2 --session 13f143b1-a2c8-4d40-9d48-ab2ed2eaa717`. Task 2 was done as commit de339c7 "feat: b". It ran only after I sent "yes, go ahead" following a second hand-back. The ledger (progress.md) has 'Task 2: base 6baf175', 'Task 2: implementer ... branch worktree-parallel-session-2)' and 'Task 2: complete ...', but no line starting with 'Task 2: branch'.

Counting `--takeover` across all Bash commands in the session log returned 0. Task 1 was claimed once without takeover: `sdd-state claim ... 1 --session 13f143b1-...`, which returned 'status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ... exit=4'.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before taking Task 2 (apart from a takeover question answered as scripted)
criteria.evidence: Right after the held result for Task 1, the agent asked an AskUserQuestion, 'Task split': "What should this second session do?" The options were Take Task 2 / Take over Task 1 / Wait, and the agent said "I need your decision before dispatching anything." After my scripted answer it handed back again: "Your answer didn't say whether I should do Task 2, so I haven't claimed it... Say 'take Task 2' and I'll claim it." That is a stop before claiming Task 2, beyond a takeover question.
